question: Why not just use two separate if statements instead of elif when only one branch should run?
answer: Two separate if statements are evaluated independently, so if more than one condition is true both blocks can run. An elif is only tested when the previous if (or elif) was false, guaranteeing that exactly one branch of the chain is executed. This prevents unintended multiple updates (e.g., both score adjustments running when the score is 60) and ensures only a single path is taken. [openstax-python-p111-c02] [openstax-python-p111-c03]
